findings.oracle: Real .hexpat source driven through the full interpreter (preprocessor/lexer/parser/evaluator) against bytes(range(256)); two independent oracles back every test: a value-oracle that branches `if (v == hand-computed-constant)` so a broken operator selects the wrong-named branch (asserted via exact `_names(results)` ordered equality), plus an offset-plus-byte oracle asserting exact `offset` AND `raw_bytes==[N]`/`display_value` read back from the computed address (byte@N==N), giving a second witness; e.g. 10-3 asserts names==['correct'] with offset 70 and raw_bytes [70], not the sum-branch; division-by-zero asserts the specific HexPatRuntimeError message; promotion/cast/precedence/wrap cases assert the exact computed value, not mere existence.
